newsitem.title: WESTERN EUROPE: W.Europe crop conditions/harvest progress.
newsitem.headline: W.Europe crop conditions/harvest progress.

text.p: Following are latest crop conditons and news on the progress of grain harvesting in the main Western European grain growing countries.

Aug 7 - Next 10-12 days crucial for wheat quality in southern England. Rain delaying harvesting Yields overall probably not too bad. But farmers concerned too much rain would shift more wheat into feed category. More rain forecast in the next couple of days, but has not been accompanied by wind, so not too many crops knocked down. But there were problems with fungus, triggered by damp. Worst hit area south-west, where heavy rain halted harvesting in most places.

Aug 6 - Wheat harvesting in south moved slowly in recent days with frequent disruptions from rain. Heavy rain halted the cereals harvest in southwest England. Localised flooding predicted. Heavy rain throughout the region, except for Cornwall, Wednesday morning. South Wales also affected. Some barley still to be harvested, wheat quality deteriorating. Most barley cut in eastern counties of Norfolk and Cambridgeshire, while more rain meant farmers further west had more left to clear. Results on barley look down on last year. 1996 UK barley crop 7.78 million tonnes. Area planted for 1997 crop for the UK as a whole was up by 5.7 percent at 1.338 million hectares. Much of the wheat still showing green straw. Early cut wheat yields down.

Aug 7 - Tail-end of three days of bad weather kept grain harvest idle in northern France but storms mostly moved south where wheat and barley have been cut. Most of the big-yielding northern areas still to be harvested have been caught up in this week's storms, boosting fears among farmers over crop damage or quality losses. But brighter weather reached into the Paris grain belt Thursday afternoon. Weather service predicted more fine spells on Friday.

Aug 5 - Grain harvesting north of the Seine halted by rain. Rain in the Paris grain regions disrupted field work and scattered thundery showers stopped the harvest altogether. Some talk of potential damage to quality and quantity north of Paris. But no suggestion that localized damage enough to alter outlook for what promises to be another large crop, especially feed grain. Harvest working its way north and crossed the river Seine for both wheat and barley.

July 24 - Soft wheat harvest 75-80 percent complete in Bourgogne Franche-Comte, eastern France, initial cuts suggest June rain and July showers hit yields and quality. More showers forecast also expected to slow progress, possibly worsen conditions. Harvest may drag into August. Winter barley better because already mature when rain hit, harvest 98 percent complete.

July 21 - Farmers start soft wheat harvest at end of month in Picardie region but officials predict June rain hit yields. Barley harvesting in north making quick progress but reports from Picardie suggest crop suffered from spring drought. Somme, Oise and Aisne - barley harvest started around July 7, 60-70 of winter crop cut. Initial results showed that despite substantial rain in May and June crop did not fully recover from drought. Yields widely seen lower. But 10 percent rise in area so larger crop in prospect.

Aug 7 - Sunny weather since Sunday allowed speedy harvesting, farmers hope to complete bulk of grain harvest in next fortnight. Barley harvest mostly complete, yields range up to 10 percent above or below last year's average 5.61 tph. Mecklenburg, Brandenburg and Saxony state, which last year had extremely bad winter barley yields, reported much improved results. Spring barley looks average. Farmers hoping spring barley would qualify for malting reported desirable low protein counts, but too early to gener alise. Winter wheat being cut in southwest but too early to assess yield and quality. Weather forecast - max. day temperatures 28-30 degrees to Aug 13, some rain.

Aug 6 - Farmers in most northerly state Schleswig-Holstein reported higher winter barley yields. More than 90 percent of barley harvested amid good weather, following frequent rain in July. Rye, winter wheat and spring barley need another fortnight to mature. Winter barley yields were in 6.00-10.00 tonne per hectare range compared with 6.82 last year in Schleswig-Holstein and 5.61 German average for 1996. winter barley area 69,949 hectares down from 72,066 last year when harvest 491,300 tonnes. Barley moi sture up to 19 percent and had to be dried down to 15 percent.

Aug 6 - Three weeks of floods in Brandenburg state threatened financial survival of 30 farms on a total of 12,000 hectares. Some 7,200 ha submerged in Ziltendorfer basin area near Neuzelle. Another 4,500 ha in Oderbruch, low-lying region below the swollen Oder river, too soaked to allow harvesting of crops this year. Ground water levels would remain high for the near future and autumn plantings for the 1998 harvest would almost certainly be imp malting properties harvested with 10-11 percent protein in Saar, 11.5 percent Rhineland, 9-11 percent in Baden-Wuerttenberg and 9-11.5 percent Baden. Bavaria malting qualities rare. Farmers in other southern states nearly completed barley harvest, yields medium to good. In east Thuringia completed 50 percent of barley harvest, yields 4.00-8.00 tph. Saxony reported 5.6-10.0 tph.

Aug 1 - Farm work on 20,000 to 30,000 hectares of crop and grazing land in eastern state of Brandenburg impossible because of high groundwater. Swamped acreage, unaccessible after two weeks of floods and heavy rain, added to 15,000 hectares farmland already totally submerged.

Aug 7 - Flooding and heavy rain which hit parts of Ireland may be big problem for individual cereal growers, but unlikely the flooding will have any impact on the national tonnage. Winter barley harvested, but no wheat or spring crops so far. Cereals crop forecast around two million tonnes, down 130,000 tonnes on 1996's bumper level. Some 307,000 hectares planted to grain, up on 1996. But yields would fall short of the record levels seen last year.
